en.title: Friend Recommendations by Mutual Friend Count
en.description:
Users are numbered 1..n. For each person, recommend one user who is neither the person themselves nor an existing friend, preferring the most mutual friends and then the smallest number; if there is no candidate, output −1. Under the statement's candidate condition of "not a friend", a user with 0 mutual friends can also be recommended. The original example used 0-based numbering; this site converts it uniformly to 1-based numbering.

The standard input/output format was compiled by CSWork; value ranges marked "this site" are this site's judging conventions.
en.input: The first line contains n m, followed by m lines of distinct undirected friendship edges u v. 1≤n≤100000, 0≤m≤250000, there are no self-loops, and each person has at most 15 friends.
en.output: Output n integers in the order of users 1..n: the user recommended for each; −1 if there is no candidate.
en.explanation: Example 1: user 1 has no candidate; 2 and 3 both know 1, so the result is −1 3 2. Example 2: there are no friendships, so every candidate has 0 mutual friends; choosing the smallest number gives 2 1 1 1. Example 3: there is only the user themselves and no candidate, so the output is −1.
hints: Iterate over the friends of friends of each person and count all non-friend candidates; if there is a positive count, pick the best by count and then by number. If there is no positive count, just find the smallest number that is neither the person nor a friend.
